description: Parity jobs for the 2026-10-07 engine extensions: longitudinal virtual patients (patients.longitudinal), the assurance of a group-sequential design, and single-arm simulation of a mean and of a survival time against a benchmark (design.simulate / design.grid 1.2.0), with the replays the earlier versions must still accept. A file of its own, read by the domain test and by the engine case N49a, so the two languages' verdicts are held equal.

valid.name: longitudinal: a trajectory over five visits with random effects and dropout
longitudinal: covariate effects from a stored population
longitudinal: the minimum a scenario states
assurance: a group-sequential design with Pocock spending and two-sided analysis
assurance: the fixed design, kind spelt out
assurance: a fixed design recorded at 1.0.0 is still valid (a replay)
simulate: single arm, a mean, one-sample t
simulate: single arm, a mean, one-sample z, two-sided null
simulate: single arm, a survival time, one-sample log-rank
simulate: single arm, a survival time against a Weibull benchmark
simulate: the binary single arm recorded at 1.1.0 is still valid (a replay)
simulate: a two-arm design recorded at 1.1.0 and one at 1.0.0 are still valid (replays)
simulate: a two-arm design recorded at 1.0.0
simulate: a group-sequential design recorded at 1.1.0
grid: single arm, a mean, over sample sizes and effects

invalid.name: longitudinal: no effect stated (a typo must not read as no effect)
longitudinal: a key the engine does not read
longitudinal: the dropout as an object, which is not a key

longitudinal: visits out of order

longitudinal: a binary endpoint
longitudinal: a residual SD of zero

longitudinal: a negative random-slope SD
longitudinal: everybody leaves
longitudinal: no treated patients
longitudinal: a version the build does not have
assurance: a group-sequential design for a continuous endpoint
assurance: a group-sequential design without its looks
assurance: looks that do not end at one
assurance: a spending function the engine does not have
assurance: looks given to a fixed design
assurance: a group-sequential design labelled with the version before it existed
assurance: a single-arm design
simulate: a z analysis without the SD it takes as known
simulate: an exact binomial analysis of a mean
simulate: a one-sample t analysis of a binary endpoint
simulate: a baseline correlation on a trial with no baseline
simulate: response rates on a mean
simulate: no alternative
simulate: one-sided analysis of a two-sided alternative
simulate: two arm sizes on a single-arm trial
simulate: both a benchmark median and a benchmark distribution
simulate: single arm on a mean labelled 1.1.0, before it existed
simulate: single arm on a survival time labelled 1.1.0

simulate: Simon two-stage on a survival time
